ch35.note: Liu Peichu, commander of the special-operations Pacification Corps and author of the posthumously published memoir Chen renders here as 'Fleeting Glimpses of a Floating Life,' which he quotes at length as his source for how the corps was formed.

Huang Fu (黄郛, 1880–1936), courtesy name Yingbai, a Nationalist diplomat-administrator who chaired the Beiping Political Readjustment Council in the mid-1930s and negotiated the uneasy accommodations with Japan, including the 1933 Tanggu Truce.
Luo Ronghuan (罗荣桓, 1902–1963), the Communist political commissar of the Northeast forces—ranking above the field commander Lin Biao—and later one of the ten marshals of the People's Republic.

The Three-Anti campaign (三反, 1951–52) was a Communist mass drive against corruption, waste, and bureaucratism among officials; its companion Five-Anti turned on private businessmen. Such campaigns swept up many former Nationalist personnel.

The Suppression of Counter-revolutionaries (镇反, about 1950–51), a nationwide Communist campaign to hunt down and execute former Nationalist agents, officers, and other reckoned enemies of the new state—the fate of several of the men named in this chapter's close.

A 'death sentence with reprieve' (死缓, sihuan) is a distinctive Chinese Communist penalty: death suspended for two years, and, if the condemned commits no further offense in that time, ordinarily commuted to imprisonment.
